records.source: וַיְהִ֣י הַגּוֹרָ֗ל לְמַטֵּ֛ה בְּנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֑ם אֶל־גְּב֨וּל אֱד֧וֹם מִדְבַּר־צִ֛ן נֶ֖גְבָּה מִקְצֵ֥ה תֵימָֽן׃
records.gloss: And was the lot for [the] tribe of [the] sons of Judah by their clans to [the] border of Edom, [the] wilderness of Zin southward, at [the] end of [the] south.
pieces: The land that fell by lot to the tribe of Judah, clan by clan, reached south to the border of Edom and the wilderness of Zin, at the far southern end.

L.1: And the lot for the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah by their clans was to the border of Edom, the wilderness of Zin southward, at the end of the south.

R.1: This is the land that the tribe of Judah received by lot for its clans. In the south it reached the border of Edom and the Zin Desert, at the land's farthest southern point.

decisions.choice: the lot: the share of land given by casting lots
decisions.reason: The land west of the Jordan was shared out by lot, so that the LORD, not the leaders, decided which tribe received which region (14:1-2; Numbers 26:55-56; 34:13). Judah's share is described first: its borders (verses 1-12), Caleb's portion (verses 13-19) and its towns (verses 20-63).

decisions.choice: was to the border of Edom: its share reached as far as Edom
decisions.reason: The verse names the southern limit of Judah's land: Edom's border and the wilderness of Zin, the same southern line that Numbers 34:3 gives for the whole land. Verses 2-4 then trace it in detail.

decisions.choice: The land that fell by lot (B); received by lot (R); the tribe of Judah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the lot ... was to the border of Edom", meaning the land the lot gave. Balanced and Readable say so. Literal keeps "children of Judah"; Balanced and Readable say "the tribe of Judah", since the tribe is meant.

decisions.choice: the Zin Desert
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 34:3.

records.heading: The borders of Judah

records.source: וַיְהִ֤י לָהֶם֙ גְּב֣וּל נֶ֔גֶב מִקְצֵ֖ה יָ֣ם הַמֶּ֑לַח מִן־הַלָּשֹׁ֖ן הַפֹּנֶ֥ה נֶֽגְבָּה׃
records.gloss: And was for them [the] border [of the] south from [the] end of [the] Sea of the Salt, from the tongue that faces southward.
pieces: Their southern border ran from the end of the Dead Sea, from the bay that faces south.

L.2: And their southern border was from the end of the Salt Sea, from the tongue that faces southward.

R.2: Their southern border began at the southern end of the Dead Sea, at the inlet that points south.

decisions.choice: the Salt Sea: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The Salt Sea is the Dead Sea, as in Numbers 34:3 and Genesis 14:3. The southern border starts at its southern end.

decisions.choice: the tongue: a bay or inlet of the sea
decisions.reason: "Tongue" is used for a strip of water reaching into the land (Isaiah 11:15). Here it is the shallow southern end of the Dead Sea, which points south; verse 5 uses the same word for the bay at its northern end.

decisions.choice: Salt Sea (L), Dead Sea (B, R); tongue (L), bay (B), inlet (R)
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 34:3, Balanced and Readable use the modern name of the sea. Literal keeps the picture of the "tongue"; Balanced and Readable say what it is.

records.source: וְ֠יָצָא אֶל־מִנֶּ֜גֶב לְמַעֲלֵ֤ה עַקְרַבִּים֙ וְעָ֣בַר צִ֔נָה וְעָלָ֥ה מִנֶּ֖גֶב לְקָדֵ֣שׁ בַּרְנֵ֑עַ וְעָבַ֤ר חֶצְרוֹן֙ וְעָלָ֣ה אַדָּ֔רָה וְנָסַ֖ב הַקַּרְקָֽעָה׃
records.gloss: And goes out to from [the] south to [the] ascent of Akrabbim, and passes on to Zin, and goes up from [the] south to Kadesh-barnea, and passes on [to] Hezron, and goes up to Addar, and turns to the Karka,
pieces: It goes out south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, passes along to Zin, goes up south of Kadesh-barnea, passes Hezron, goes up to Addar and turns toward Karka,

L.3: And it goes out south of the ascent of Akrabbim, and passes on to Zin, and goes up south of Kadesh-barnea, and passes on to Hezron, and goes up to Addar, and turns to Karka,

R.3: From there it went south of Scorpion Pass and on to Zin. Then it went up south of Kadesh-barnea, past Hezron and up to Addar, and turned toward Karka.

decisions.choice: went out, passed on, went up: the course of the line
decisions.reason: The verbs trace the border from one landmark to the next, as if walking along it. They describe how the line runs on the ground, as in Numbers 34:4-5.

decisions.choice: the ascent of Akrabbim: the Scorpions' Pass
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 34:4: a road climbing steeply up from the desert south-west of the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: Hezron, Addar, Karka: places on the southern edge
decisions.reason: Numbers 34:4 has Hazar-addar where this verse names Hezron and Addar, perhaps two settlements near one another. Karka is named only here. None of the three sites is known for certain.

decisions.choice: the Ascent of Akrabbim (B); Scorpion Pass (R)
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 34:4.

decisions.choice: goes out ... turns (L, B); went ... turned (R)
decisions.reason: The border is traced with a chain of verbs in a form that describes how a line regularly runs. Literal and Balanced use the present tense for it, as through the boundary lists of chapters 15-19 (18:12). Readable tells the line in the past tense, as part of the story of the lot; the sense is the same.

records.source: וְעָבַ֣ר עַצְמ֗וֹנָה וְיָצָא֙ נַ֣חַל מִצְרַ֔יִם וְהָי֛וּ תֹּצְא֥וֹת הַגְּב֖וּל יָ֑מָּה זֶה־יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם גְּב֥וּל נֶֽגֶב׃
records.gloss: and passes on [to] Azmon, and goes out [to the] wadi of Egypt, and are [the] ends of the border at [the] sea. This will be for you [the] border [of the] south.
pieces: passes Azmon, and goes out to the Wadi of Egypt, ending at the sea. This will be your southern border.

L.4: and passes on to Azmon, and goes out to the brook of Egypt; and the end of the border is at the sea. This will be your southern border.

R.4: It passed Azmon and went to the Wadi of Egypt, a stream that is dry most of the year. It ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This will be your southern border.

decisions.choice: the wadi of Egypt: the stream bed between Canaan and Egypt
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 34:5. It lay in the desert of northern Sinai and marked the edge of Canaan toward Egypt (verse 47).

decisions.choice: this will be your southern border: the words of the command repeated
decisions.reason: The sentence speaks to Israel as "you", in the words the LORD gave Moses for the borders of the whole land (Numbers 34:3-6). The writer quotes the command to show that Judah's southern border is the border promised there. The ancient Greek translation reads "their southern border".

decisions.choice: they are: the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text read "it is"; the reading the scribes marked to be read, followed here, is "they are", agreeing with the plural "ends". The meaning is the same, as in Numbers 34:4.

decisions.choice: brook (L), Wadi (B, R); the Mediterranean Sea (R)
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 34:5. Readable explains the wadi and names the sea.

records.source: וּגְב֥וּל קֵ֨דְמָה֙ יָ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לַח עַד־קְצֵ֖ה הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וּגְב֞וּל לִפְאַ֤ת צָפ֨וֹנָה֙ מִלְּשׁ֣וֹן הַיָּ֔ם מִקְצֵ֖ה הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And [the] border eastward [is] the Sea of the Salt to [the] end of the Jordan. And [the] border on [the] side northward [is] from [the] tongue of the sea, from [the] end of the Jordan.
pieces: On the east, the Dead Sea forms the border, up to the mouth of the Jordan. On the north side the border begins at the bay where the Jordan enters the sea.

L.5: And the eastern border [is] the Salt Sea, as far as the end of the Jordan. And the border on the north side [is] from the tongue of the sea, at the end of the Jordan.

R.5: On the east, the border was the Dead Sea, all the way up to where the Jordan River flows into it. The northern border began at the bay at the north end of the Dead Sea, where the Jordan flows in.

decisions.choice: the end of the Jordan: where the river flows into the sea
decisions.reason: The "end" of the river is its mouth, the place where it empties into the Dead Sea. The whole western shore of the sea is Judah's eastern border.

decisions.choice: the tongue of the sea: the bay at the northern end
decisions.reason: The same word as in verse 2, here for the bay at the north end of the Dead Sea, where the Jordan comes in. The northern border starts from there and runs west (verses 6-11).
The Hebrew sets the border beside the place without a verb. Literal supplies "is" in brackets.

decisions.choice: the mouth of the Jordan (B); where the Jordan River flows into it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "end" of the river is (m1). Literal keeps "end".

records.source: וְעָלָ֤ה הַגְּבוּל֙ בֵּ֣ית חָגְלָ֔ה וְעָבַ֕ר מִצְּפ֖וֹן לְבֵ֣ית הָעֲרָבָ֑ה וְעָלָ֣ה הַגְּב֔וּל אֶ֥בֶן בֹּ֖הַן בֶּן־רְאוּבֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And goes up the border [to] Beth-hoglah, and passes on from [the] north of Beth-arabah, and goes up the border [to the] stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
pieces: The border goes up to Beth-hoglah and passes north of Beth-arabah, then goes up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

L.6: And the border goes up to Beth-hoglah, and passes on north of Beth-arabah; and the border goes up to the stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

R.6: From there it went up to Beth-hoglah and passed north of Beth-arabah. Then it went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben, a rock that served as a landmark.

decisions.choice: Beth-hoglah and Beth-arabah: places in the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: Both lay in the valley near Jericho, between the river and the hills. The same line is the southern border of Benjamin (18:19-22), and Beth-arabah is counted among Judah's towns in verse 61 and among Benjamin's in 18:22.

decisions.choice: the stone of Bohan son of Reuben: a known landmark
decisions.reason: The stone is named only here and in 18:17. Why it bore the name of a man from the tribe of Reuben is not told; it was a rock well known enough to mark the line.

decisions.choice: a rock that served as a landmark
decisions.reason: Readable says why a stone is named in a border list (m2).

records.source: וְעָלָ֨ה הַגְּב֥וּל׀דְּבִרָה֮ מֵעֵ֣מֶק עָכוֹר֒ וְצָפ֜וֹנָה פֹּנֶ֣ה אֶל־הַגִּלְגָּ֗ל אֲשֶׁר־נֹ֨כַח֙ לְמַעֲלֵ֣ה אֲדֻמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִנֶּ֖גֶב לַנָּ֑חַל וְעָבַ֤ר הַגְּבוּל֙ אֶל־מֵי־עֵ֣ין שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ וְהָי֥וּ תֹצְאֹתָ֖יו אֶל־עֵ֥ין רֹגֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And goes up the border to Debir from [the] valley of Achor, and northward turning to the Gilgal which [is] opposite [the] ascent of Adummim, which [is] south of the wadi; and passes on the border to [the] waters of En-shemesh, and are its ends at En-rogel.
pieces: From the Valley of Achor the border goes up to Debir and turns north toward Gilgal, which faces the Ascent of Adummim, on the south side of the wadi. It goes on to the waters of En-shemesh and comes out at En-rogel.

L.7: And the border goes up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, and turning northward to Gilgal, which [is] opposite the ascent of Adummim, which [is] south of the wadi; and the border passes on to the waters of En-shemesh, and its end is at En-rogel.

R.7: From the Valley of Achor it went up to Debir and turned north toward Gilgal. Gilgal is across from the road that climbs to Adummim, south of the stream bed. Then the border went on to the springs of En-shemesh and reached En-rogel.

decisions.choice: Debir and the Valley of Achor: places in the hills west of Jericho
decisions.reason: This Debir is a place on the northern border, not the town Caleb's family took (verse 15). The Valley of Achor is where Achan was put to death (7:24-26).

decisions.choice: Gilgal opposite the ascent of Adummim
decisions.reason: Adummim means "red places", probably from the color of the rocks; the ascent is the road climbing from the Jordan valley toward Jerusalem. This Gilgal faces it and may be the Geliloth of 18:17. It is not certainly the camp near Jericho (4:19).

decisions.choice: En-shemesh and En-rogel: springs east and south of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: En means "spring": En-shemesh is "spring of the sun", on the road east of Jerusalem. En-rogel was a spring in the valley just below the city, where David's messengers hid and Adonijah held his feast (2 Samuel 17:17; 1 Kings 1:9).

decisions.choice: the road that climbs to Adummim; the stream bed; the springs
decisions.reason: Readable says what the "ascent", the "wadi" and the "waters" are.

records.source: וְעָלָ֨ה הַגְּב֜וּל גֵּ֣י בֶן־הִנֹּ֗ם אֶל־כֶּ֤תֶף הַיְבוּסִי֙ מִנֶּ֔גֶב הִ֖יא יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְעָלָ֨ה הַגְּב֜וּל אֶל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֗ר אֲ֠שֶׁר עַל־פְּנֵ֤י גֵֽי־הִנֹּם֙ יָ֔מָּה אֲשֶׁ֛ר בִּקְצֵ֥ה עֵֽמֶק־רְפָאִ֖ים צָפֹֽנָה׃
records.gloss: And goes up the border [by the] valley of Ben-hinnom to [the] slope of the Jebusite from [the] south, that [is] Jerusalem; and goes up the border to [the] top of the mountain which [is] on [the] face of [the] valley of Hinnom westward, which [is] at [the] end of [the] valley of Rephaim northward.
pieces: Then the border goes up the Valley of Ben-hinnom along the southern slope of the Jebusite city, that is, Jerusalem. From there it goes up to the hilltop that looks across the Valley of Hinnom from the west, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim.

L.8: And the border goes up by the Valley of Ben-hinnom to the slope of the Jebusite on the south, that [is] Jerusalem; and the border goes up to the top of the mountain that [is] facing the Valley of Hinnom westward, which [is] at the end of the Valley of Rephaim northward.

R.8: Next it went up the Valley of Ben-hinnom, along the south side of the hill where the Jebusites lived, that is, Jerusalem. Then it climbed to the top of the hill that looks across the Valley of Hinnom from the west. That hill is at the north end of the Valley of Rephaim.

decisions.choice: the slope of the Jebusite: the hillside of the Jebusite city
decisions.reason: "The Jebusite" stands for the people and their town, which is Jerusalem. "Slope" is literally "shoulder", the side of a hill (Numbers 34:11). The line runs along the south side of the city, so Jerusalem itself lies just outside Judah, in Benjamin (18:16, 28).

decisions.choice: the Valley of Ben-hinnom: "the valley of the son of Hinnom"
decisions.reason: The valley ran along the south and west of Jerusalem and was named after a man called Hinnom. It later became a place of child sacrifice and a byword for judgment (2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 7:31-32); its name, Ge-hinnom, is the source of Gehenna.

decisions.choice: the Valley of Rephaim: a broad valley south-west of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The name recalls the Rephaim, a people of great size who once lived in the land (Deuteronomy 2:11). The Philistines later camped there to attack David (2 Samuel 5:18, 22).

decisions.choice: the Jebusite city (B); the hill where the Jebusites lived (R); hill for "mountain"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the Jebusite" means here (m1). The word for "mountain" is used for any high ground; around Jerusalem it is a hill.

records.source: וְתָאַ֨ר הַגְּב֜וּל מֵרֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֗ר אֶל־מַעְיַן֙ מֵ֣י נֶפְתּ֔וֹחַ וְיָצָ֖א אֶל־עָרֵ֣י הַר־עֶפְר֑וֹן וְתָאַ֤ר הַגְּבוּל֙ בַּעֲלָ֔ה הִ֖יא קִרְיַ֥ת יְעָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And turns the border from [the] top of the mountain to [the] spring of [the] waters of Nephtoah, and goes out to [the] cities of Mount Ephron; and turns the border [to] Baalah, that [is] Kiriath-jearim.
pieces: From the top of the hill the border curves around to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, goes out to the towns of Mount Ephron, and bends around to Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim.

L.9: And the border is drawn from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, and goes out to the cities of Mount Ephron; and the border is drawn to Baalah, that [is] Kiriath-jearim.

R.9: From the top of that hill the border turned toward the spring called the Waters of Nephtoah and went out to the towns of Mount Ephron. Then it turned toward Baalah, which is also called Kiriath-jearim.

decisions.choice: the spring of the waters of Nephtoah; Mount Ephron
decisions.reason: A spring north-west of Jerusalem and a range of hills beyond it, named again on Benjamin's border (18:15). Their exact sites are not certain.

decisions.choice: Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim
decisions.reason: Kiriath-jearim, "town of forests", was one of the Gibeonite towns (9:17) and later the place where the ark stayed for twenty years (1 Samuel 7:1-2). Baalah, a name formed from Baal, was its older name; verse 60 calls it Kiriath-baal.

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: The word for "city" is used of any walled place where people live, however small. Balanced and Readable say "towns"; Literal keeps "cities", as in Numbers 32:16.

records.source: וְנָסַב֩ הַגְּב֨וּל מִבַּעֲלָ֥ה יָ֨מָּה֙ אֶל־הַ֣ר שֵׂעִ֔יר וְעָבַ֕ר אֶל־כֶּ֧תֶף הַר־יְעָרִ֛ים מִצָּפ֖וֹנָה הִ֣יא כְסָל֑וֹן וְיָרַ֥ד בֵּֽית־שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ וְעָבַ֥ר תִּמְנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And turns the border from Baalah westward to Mount Seir, and passes on to [the] slope of Mount Jearim from [the] north, that [is] Chesalon; and goes down [to] Beth-shemesh, and passes on [to] Timnah.
pieces: From Baalah the border turns west to Mount Seir, passes along the northern slope of Mount Jearim, that is, Chesalon, then goes down to Beth-shemesh and on to Timnah.

L.10: And the border turns from Baalah westward to Mount Seir, and passes on to the slope of Mount Jearim on the north, that [is] Chesalon; and goes down to Beth-shemesh, and passes on to Timnah.

R.10: From Baalah it turned west to Mount Seir. It went along the north side of Mount Jearim, that is, Chesalon. Then it went down to Beth-shemesh and on to Timnah.

decisions.choice: Mount Seir: a ridge west of Kiriath-jearim
decisions.reason: This is a hill on Judah's northern border, not the mountain country of Edom that has the same name (Genesis 36:8).

decisions.choice: Mount Jearim, Chesalon, Beth-shemesh, Timnah
decisions.reason: "That is Chesalon" names the place on the slope of Mount Jearim ("forested mountain"). Beth-shemesh, "house of the sun", is the town where the ark came back from the Philistines (1 Samuel 6:12-15), and Timnah is the town where Samson found his wife (Judges 14:1).

records.source: וְיָצָ֨א הַגְּב֜וּל אֶל־כֶּ֣תֶף עֶקְרוֹן֮ צָפוֹנָה֒ וְתָאַ֤ר הַגְּבוּל֙ שִׁכְּר֔וֹנָה וְעָבַ֥ר הַר־הַֽבַּעֲלָ֖ה וְיָצָ֣א יַבְנְאֵ֑ל וְהָי֛וּ תֹּצְא֥וֹת הַגְּב֖וּל יָֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: And goes out the border to [the] slope of Ekron northward, and bends the border [to] Shikkeron, and passes on [to] Mount the Baalah, and goes out [to] Jabneel; and are [the] ends of the border at [the] sea.
pieces: The border goes out to the slope north of Ekron, curves around to Shikkeron, passes along to Mount Baalah and goes out to Jabneel. It ends at the sea.

L.11: And the border goes out to the slope of Ekron northward, and the border is drawn to Shikkeron, and passes on to Mount Baalah, and goes out to Jabneel; and the end of the border is at the sea.

R.11: It went on to the hillside north of Ekron and curved around to Shikkeron. Then it passed Mount Baalah, went on to Jabneel and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.

decisions.choice: Ekron, Shikkeron, Mount Baalah, Jabneel: the last stretch to the coast
decisions.reason: Ekron was one of the five Philistine cities (13:3). Shikkeron is named only here. Mount Baalah is a ridge near the coast, not the Baalah of verse 9. Jabneel is probably the later Jabneh, near the sea (2 Chronicles 26:6).

decisions.choice: the Mediterranean Sea
decisions.reason: Readable names the sea, as in verse 4.

records.source: וּגְב֣וּל יָ֔ם הַיָּ֥מָּה הַגָּד֖וֹל וּגְב֑וּל זֶ֠ה גְּב֧וּל בְּנֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֛ה סָבִ֖יב לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And [the] border [of the] west [is] to the sea, the great, and [its] border. This [is the] border of [the] sons of Judah around by their clans.
pieces: The western border is the Great Sea and its coast. These are the borders of the people of Judah on every side, clan by clan.

L.12: And the western border [is] the Great Sea and [its] coast. This [is] the border of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah all around, by their clans.

R.12: On the west, the border was the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. Those were the borders all around the land of the tribe of Judah, for all its clans.

decisions.choice: the Great Sea and its coast: the Mediterranean shore
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 34:6: the sea itself, with its coastline, is the western border.

decisions.choice: this is the border all around: the summary that closes the description
decisions.reason: The words answer verse 1: the land inside the four lines, south (verses 2-4), east (verse 5), north (verses 5-11) and west (verse 12), is the share of Judah's clans.

decisions.choice: the people of Judah (B); the tribe of Judah (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "children of Judah". Balanced and Readable name the people as a tribe; the Hebrew phrase means the descendants of Judah, men and women.

records.gloss: and the Nibshan and the City of the Salt and En-gedi: cities six, and their villages.
pieces: Nibshan, the City of Salt and En-gedi: six towns and their villages.

L.62: and Nibshan and the City of Salt and En-gedi: six cities and their villages.

R.62: Nibshan, the City of Salt and En-gedi. In all, there were six towns with their villages.

decisions.choice: Nibshan, the City of Salt, En-gedi
decisions.reason: The City of Salt lay near the Dead Sea, as its name says. En-gedi ("spring of the young goat") is an oasis on the sea's western shore, where David hid from Saul (1 Samuel 24:1-2). The Hebrew calls the first "the Nibshan".

decisions.choice: six cities (L), towns (B, R), and their villages
decisions.reason: As in verse 32: each group of towns closes with the same count, in the same words.

records.gloss: And the Jebusite[s], [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, not were able [the] sons of Judah to dispossess them; and has dwelt the Jebusite with [the] sons of Judah in Jerusalem until the day the this.
pieces: But the people of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, who lived in Jerusalem, and the Jebusites live there with the people of Judah to this day.

L.63: And the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem — the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah were not able to dispossess them; and the Jebusites have lived with the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.

R.63: But the people of Judah were not able to drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem. So the Jebusites still live there among the people of Judah today.

decisions.choice: the Jebusites in Jerusalem: a city not taken
decisions.reason: Jerusalem lay on the border with Benjamin (verse 8; 18:16, 28), and neither tribe took it (Judges 1:21). Judges 1:8 tells of Judah burning part of it, but the Jebusites kept their stronghold until David captured it (2 Samuel 5:6-9).

decisions.choice: to this day: up to the time of writing
decisions.reason: The phrase speaks from the writer's own time. The Jebusites were still living in Jerusalem, among the people of Judah, in the writer's day.

decisions.choice: they were able: the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The written consonants and the reading the scribes marked differ only in the form of the verb "were able"; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: And the Jebusites ... — the children of Judah were not able
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the Jebusites first for emphasis and then starts the sentence again. Literal shows this with a dash; Balanced and Readable make one sentence.

decisions.choice: But (B, R); So (R)
decisions.reason: The opening "and" sets this against the list of towns Judah received, so Balanced and Readable say "But". Readable makes the result clear with "So".
